title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Volunteer 

& 

Visitor 

Policy Volunteer & Visitor Policy

As we continue with our volunteer policy this year, please remember that any adult volunteer who wishes to enter the school building must have a volunteer application on file with the office every school year. After a parent’s second visit to the building, or if they plan to chaperone, assist with a field trip, they are required to complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office. Please plan to complete this process at least 3 weeks prior to the event. This allows adequate time for the background check to be completed and for the appropriate information to be provided to the school administrator for planning purposes. Once completed, your background check is valid for 5 years.Central Registration Office:Ruth Michael📞 513-273-3101We appreciate your understanding and cooperation as we work to keep our students, staff, and school community safe. Public schools have implemented these regulations to comply with state and federal safety requirements regarding volunteers and visitors in schools.Thank you for helping us make safety a priority at Kramer Elementary! ❤️

summary: All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file each school year. After a second visit or before chaperoning/assisting with field trips, volunteers must complete **fingerprinting and background check** through the Central Registration Office at least **3 weeks prior** to the event. Background checks are valid for 5 years. Contact **Ruth Michael at 513-273-3101** for Central Registration.

title: PAX Good Behavior Program Information
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: PAX PAX

summary:
**PAX Vision** is a school-wide behavior program that helps set clear expectations for student conduct. PAX refers to anything that adds to Peace, Productivity, Health, and Happiness, while Spleems are behaviors that detract from these values. 

The program teaches students to:
- **See More** smiling, **Hear More** nice words, **Do More** taking turns, and **Feel More** happy
- **See Less** running, **Hear Less** shouting, **Do Less** interrupting, and **Feel Less** nervous

Parents can engage by asking their child: What did everyone want more of in PAX Vision today? What PAX things did you and friends do well? What Spleems is everyone still working on?

title: Peachjar Digital Flyer System Launching
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Peachjar Peachjar

We are excited to announce a new partnership aimed at improving how we share information with you. Talawanda School District is launching Peachjar this 2026-2027 school year! Peachjar is an innovative digital flyer management system. It transitions our schools from paper handouts to electronic flyer delivery, and assists with ADA compliance to meet the new Ohio law mandates in this area.Why Are We Making the Switch?Eco-Friendly: Saves thousands of sheets of paper annually.Highly Convenient: Delivers school and community resources straight to your inbox.Accessible: View important updates anytime on your phone or computer.Saves Time: Frees up valuable administrative and classroom instruction time.What to Expect as a Parent/Community Member:You do not need to take any action to register. If your email address is on file with the district, Peachjar will automatically create an account for you.You will receive a weekly digest email containing school-approved flyers.You can view flyers by clicking the Peachjar button on our school website.Your email address is kept entirely confidential and is never shared.You can opt out or adjust your email frequency at any time.

summary: Talawanda School District is launching **Peachjar**, a digital flyer management system, for the **2026-2027 school year**. This eco-friendly platform will replace paper handouts and deliver school-approved flyers via weekly digest emails to parents. No registration is required—accounts will be automatically created using district email addresses, and flyers can also be viewed on the school website.

title: Older Americans Month Community BINGO Challenge
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached if you'd like to print one at home.

Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community are hosting **Community BINGO** to promote physical, mental, and emotional health. Pick up a BINGO card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), The Knolls of Oxford, or Scripps Gerontology Center (396 Upham Hall), complete activities throughout May, and bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on May 31, 3:00-5:00 PM** at Oxford Seniors for prizes and snacks.

title: Kramer Reading at Home Program Success
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Kramer's 

Reading 

at 

Home 

(RAH)

Kramer's Reading at Home (RAH)

This school year, Kramer’s Reading At Home (RAH) program was a huge success, and we are so proud of our students’ dedication to reading!An incredible 82% of our K–2 students participated by turning in at least one reading sheet; that’s 208 young readers building strong habits at home. Even more impressive, almost half of those participants turned in 10 or more sheets, showing consistent commitment throughout the year.Our most avid readers truly went above and beyond. We had 26 students read over 500 books, and our top three readers each surpassed an amazing 1,000 books!Altogether, Kramer students recorded over 39,000 books read this year! Each book read is an opportunity to grow imagination, vocabulary, and a lifelong love of reading.These impressive readers took home more than 1,000 books from the RAH cart, helping them build their own home libraries. Rewards also kept motivation high, with the favorite prize this year being coupons to local businesses like Oxford Doughnut Shoppe and Spring Street Treats.Thank you to our families for supporting reading at home and helping make this program such a meaningful part of our school community. We can’t wait to see even more reading adventures next year!
